data.name: Grid Masters
data.detailed_description:
Fight for victory in a 1v1 or 2v2 grid-based deathmatch in Grid Masters. Represent your favorite faction as one of five characters (with more to come), each with their own unique abilities. Toss massive bombs, rocket punch, or send explosive robot minions to take your enemies down!


Grid Masters takes place on the planet Orikos, where vast alliances, held together by bonds of convenience rather than loyalty, constantly struggle for power and influence. Nations work anonymously to sabotage both friends and enemies, while giant company blocs, called Megacorps, hover around these nations like scavengers, controlling commerce and wielding enormous power under the leadership of a mysterious council, the Directorate.

The animosity among the different nations and the Megacorps is at its strongest on the Grid. Every year, the great powers of the Orikos send their finest warrior to compete in order to prove their power. The winner’s host gains influence and notoriety, while the victor is awarded fame and fortune. The losers pay briefly with their lives before the Respawners throw them back into the fray. Who will be this year’s champion?

Grid Masters is influenced by Megaman Battle Network and Super Smash Brothers.

Game Features Currently Available
  • 5 unique characters
  • Team deathmatch mode
  • Single player and co-op arcade mode
  • Server list to find multiplayer games (in early testing)
  • Local or online play, up to 4 players!
  • Windows support
  • 4 levels of bot difficulty

Full Game Release Goals
  • Mac OS X and Linux support coming soon
  • Many more characters
  • Match mutators
  • Single player and co-op endless mode

Controller Support
  • 2 players on keyboard
  • Xbox-like gamepads
  • If demand exists, other gamepad types

reviews.review:
Grid Masters is a case of giving a game a second opportunity. The first time I played the game it was under the provision of a single player game. The game, after all, does include that mode. I didn't enjoy myself. The game was too simple and not deep enough for my liking. It just didn't offer enough gameplay value to me as a single player game. I was almost ready to write a scathing review about a game that simply shouldn't have been released. And while I still feel that the single player game is lacking - and not for a lack of trying from the developer and admittedly there is room for growth - it was under the advisement of a friend that I gave the game a second chance to woo me over as a multiplayer game.

This game was intentionally designed to be played as a multiplayer game either on a couch or online. If you are hoping for a deeply engrossing single player experience you'll likely be left disappointed as I was. However, as a couch game with buddies or hosting your own games via the game's online set up you've got a far greater likelihood of finding hours of entertainment and joy in the title.

Grid Masters works as a strategic action game played between factions. You need to carefully consider your position in your twelve slot grid. You are given powers that have different areas of effect and behave in different ways. Each character has their own set of powers. There are, as of writing, five characters with more to come. The game is heavily dependent upon strategy and button mashing will only work when you're playing someone who doesn't understand the game.

I'd like to see some story and character backgrounds provided because although the game can be fun I don't have a reason to care about any of them. That would be my largest request at this stage of development. I'm interested in seeing how development progresses along in this regard as well as the addition of the other characters. There is a lot of scope for improvement.  As an Early Access game there is a lot of development left in order for the game's potential to be fulfilled. However, it is in a playable state and is entertaining when played with friends.
